data.title: lululemon athletica's turnaround story is getting stretched thin -- analysts
data.description:
Wall Street seems to have thrown in the towel on lululemon athletica (LULU) after the company’s recent quarterly results underscored the challenges the company continues to face, namely inconsistent demand for new products, worsening comparable store sales in North America and China, public criticism by a disgruntled former CEO, and a leadership vacuum as the company operates under interim co-CEOs.

“The magnitude of decline seen at LULU feels jarring,” said Wells Fargo’s Ike Boruchow with the company’s 4th cut to its full-year guidance since last June leaving shares at an all-time low.

“With the model fully unraveling, the debate is no longer if a reset is needed but rather how low the base needs to fall,” Boruchow added.

While there is no shortage of reasons for lululemon’s (LULU) current fate—interim co-CEO Meghan Frank even blamed negative social media commentary—Oppenheimer's Brian Nagel sees the company’s top- and bottom-line weakness as “primarily a function of internal missteps in merchandising and marketing.”

On the earnings call with analysts, Frank acknowledged the “softer-than-planned” response to new product launches, competitive markets, and brand deterioration and said management is committed to “reinforcing lululemon’s premium positioning” by returning to full-price sales growth.

But the athleisure market is not what it used to be, Citi Research analyst Paul Lejuez notes, becoming more competitive with a more discerning customer, a dynamic that might not support full-priced lululemon merchandise.

With former Nike executive Heidi O’Neill taking the helm, the brand could regain its luster, but further downside in both the stock price and revenue is likely.

“Our view is reaffirmed that the path forward for LULU is no different from every softline turnaround we analyzed, requiring at a minimum a 10% decline from peak revenue and 4+ years of work before returning to growth,” Boruchow notes, keeping an Equal Weight rating on the stock.

data.title: The US and China prepare for AI safety talks mid-September: Reuters
data.description:
The United States and China are preparing for an AI safety dialogue in mid-September, Reuters reported on Friday, citing two sources. 

The talks would be the first official bilateral discussions focused exclusively on artificial intelligence between the two countries since President Donald Trump began his second term. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to lead the U.S. side, Reuters reported.

The Treasury Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha. 

The United States wants to discuss cooperation on monitoring AI-directed cyberattacks and has proposed that U.S. and Chinese AI labs share information and take steps to prevent AI-linked attacks.

The agenda and participants remain subject to change. China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng could lead the Chinese delegation, while Politburo Standing Committee member Ding Xuexiang is also being considered.

The discussions are expected to take place ahead of a planned September 24 meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington.

Recent Anthropic (ANTHRO) models have drawn attention for their ability to identify software vulnerabilities, raising concerns about the potential for advanced AI systems to be misused for cyberattacks.

There were also reports that OpenAI (OPENAI) agents hijacked a German website in the spring of 2026. OpenAI, in late August, published a technical report detailing how its AI models breached Hugging Face last month, an incident that has spooked executives and lawmakers alike.

Michael Kratsios, the science advisor to U.S. President Donald Trump, has said in July that China-based startup Moonshot AI developed its latest model, Kimi K3, through the “industrial distillation” of Anthropic's Fable. Distillation is a training method where less capable models are improved by utilizing outputs from stronger models.

data.title: Magnificent Seven breaks with momentum
data.description:
For the first time, the Magnificent Seven are moving against U.S. market momentum rather than with it.

Sherwood News compiled rolling 21-session correlations of daily price changes between the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) and the iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF (MTUM). That short-window measure has turned negative, ending the tight co-movement that defined mega-cap tech through the AI-led bull market.

MAGS provides exposure to Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Nvidia (NVDA), Amazon (AMZN), Meta (META), Alphabet (GOOG)(GOOGL) and Tesla (TSLA). MTUM holds large- and mid-cap names that have recently outperformed. For years the two baskets rose and fell together as those seven stocks anchored factor leadership and index returns. 

The inversion follows a broader rotation. Capital has shifted toward memory chips, other semiconductors, and a wider set of S&P 500 names, while the Magnificent Seven themselves have stopped trading as a single block. A negative MAGS–MTUM reading means the old leaders are no longer the engine of the momentum factor: they can lag when high-momentum stocks keep running, or hold up when that trade cools.

The signal is short-lived and can flip quickly. Still, it is a rare statistical first for a group that once set the tape.

Other Magnificent Seven Funds: (MAGX), (QQQU), and (QQQD).

data.title: Wacker Chemie's Tennessee polysilicon factory at risk of closure - Reuters
data.description:
Wacker Chemie (WKCMF) down 4.9% in Friday's trading following a Reuters report that the German company will decide in the coming weeks whether to close its polysilicon factory in Charleston, Tennessee, after the Trump administration's new trade measures that ​seek to incentivize purchases of American polysilicon wound up driving away the plant's two remaining customers.

The trade measures, ​announced August 6, include a ⁠price floor and a tariff on inbound polysilicon ingots, wafers, cells, and solar panels, but they apply equally to products made abroad with polysilicon from anywhere, treating Chinese and American-origin materials the same, a policy that critics say maintains the disadvantage for more costly U.S. polysilicon.

Wacker (WKCMF) told Reuters it is too soon to assess the policy's impact on its business ​but said the proclamation "does not, as it reads now, effectively support the use of U.S.-made polysilicon."

Wacker's (WKCMF) German and American operations have been struggling with Chinese competition; it cut jobs at the Charleston plant last year, and CEO Christian Hartel has warned that the ​company could have "one plant too many" if the expected trade action is not beneficial.

data.title: Keyera slides after cutting guidance on pipeline disruption, facility repairs
data.description:
Keyera (KEYUF) down 5.1% in Friday's trading after saying it lowered guidance for its 2026 marketing segment realized margin to C$320M-C$350M from C$360M-C$390M previously, reflecting the estimated impact of the ongoing Line 5 disruption and lower expected production at the company's Alberta EnviroFuels facility.

Keyera (KEYUF) estimated the disruption at Enbridge's Line 5 pipeline, which has been shut down since August 25 following a third-party line strike in Wisconsin, will reduce its marketing segment realized margin by ~C$30M, reflecting a combination of lost and deferred product sales; Keyera uses Line 5 to transport liquids from its Fort Saskatchewan and Empress operations to its Samia fractionation facility.

Additionally, the company said it resumed full operations at its Alberta EnviroFuels facility in June following a five-month outage during which it completed required repairs on damaged equipment, but the facility requires additional equipment replacements that will require it to operate at ~70% capacity through April 2027.

data.title: Sonida Senior Living upgraded to Buy equivalent at Baird
data.description:
Sonida Senior Living (SNDA) was trading higher as Baird Equity Research raised its recommendation on the stock to Buy equivalent.

Shares were 1.19% higher at $38.33 Friday afternoon.

"We believe SNDA is well-positioned to benefit from the highly favorable senior housing operating environment," said analyst Wesley Golladay in a research note.

"In addition, we believe the improved scale of the company and build-out of the operating platform should drive incremental returns from the existing assets and acquisitions, further bolstering the flywheel for future growth," said Golladay.

Sonida-CNL "merger integration appears to be on track and the company is looking to resume external growth. Leverage is high, but there are limited maturities through 2028, and we expect continued deleveraging via organic growth," said the note.

Baird upgraded the stock to Outperform, with the price target raised to $43 from $37.

The rating aligns with the Wall Street analysts and Seeking Alpha authors rating of Buy. The Quant Rating system sees the stock as Hold.

data.title: Wall Street slides after investors received the latest payrolls print
data.description:
Wall Street's major market averages shifted lower after traders and investors digested the latest jobs data, which came in stronger than forecasted.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last -0.4%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -0.2%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last -0.2%. 

From a sector-by-sector standpoint, just three of the 11 S&P segments were in the green and were led by industrials. At the other end, consumer discretionary was the weakest performer. 

On the economic front, the August U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased by +162K versus the +55K consensus figure, according to data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. At the same time, the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, compared to the 4.2% forecasted level. 

Treasury yields are on the move higher. The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) moved up 4 basis points to 4.38%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) was higher by 1 basis point to 4.77%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) inched up 1 basis point to 5.24%. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of KLA Corporation (KLAC) climbed higher by +8.2%, while shares of Lululemon (LULU) fell -17.5%.

data.title: Ciena appears 'primed for growth,' dip is a buying opportunity: BNP
data.description:
Despite reporting better-than-expected results and guidance earlier this week, shares of Ciena (CIEN) sold off. Investment firm BNP Paribas said investors should use the dip in the shares of the optical networking firm as it appears “primed for growth.”

“Ciena is implementing price increases ranging from high-single digits to low-20s, which we think will primarily impact FY28 results,” BNP Paribas analyst Karl Ackerman wrote in a note to clients. “We believe the ramp of Hyper-Rail RLS starting in CY27 is an additional margin tailwind. Ciena continues to drive strong leverage with FQ4 [operating margin] guided to 20% and expected to reach 26% in FY27 (333 bps above).”

Ackerman has an Outperform rating and a $640 price target on Ciena, or roughly 80% higher than current levels.

Delving deeper, Ackerman said it's plausible that Ciena obtains a 70% share of the reconfigurable line system market, and the company is executing well, as it shipped more than twice the volume of the 800G ZR pluggables compared to the second quarter. The company also received sample orders for its Vesta CPX optical engine, which supports co-packaged optics. 

“We believe Ciena can sustain over 30% revenue CAGR through CY29 with EPS approaching $24, or 3x CY26 levels,” Ackerman added.

Ciena's shares rose more than 1% on Friday.

data.title: Strong August employment revives case for Fed hike, TS Lombard says
data.description:
Stronger August employment data had reinforced the underlying uptrend in the U.S. labor market, according to TS Lombard economists led by Dario Perkins.

The analysts said recent weakness in employment growth had likely been noise, with seasonal factors having pulled payroll growth below its underlying trend before August data corrected for that weakness. Upward revisions to July had also helped preserve the broader uptrend, they said.

U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased by 162K vs. +55K consensus and +21K in the prior month (revised from -23K), according to data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics on Friday.

The economists pointed to the NFIB survey, which they said generally provided a reliable lead on employment trends, as suggesting that the pickup could continue.

A soft patch remained a risk as the effects of first-quarter tax refunds and a decline in the second-quarter savings rate shifted toward employment and wage growth. But the underlying driver, earnings growth, appeared to be broadening, according to the note.

The report argued that the data did not provide a strong reason for the Federal Reserve to hike rapidly, but that a rate increase this month had become important for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's credibility.

“Hiking this month is a must for credibility,” the economists wrote, arguing that failing to hike would leave Warsh with a difficult situation to address later.

Markets had been pricing what TS Lombard described as a “credibility hike,” a dynamic the economists said was more commonly associated with European central banking.

They cautioned, however, that the U.S. economy had a more flexible labor market and could prove more prone to inflation if growth reaccelerated. Wage growth also appeared to be picking up after excluding lower-signal sectors such as education and health, they said.

The economists said the outlook remained untested and that they saw limited evidence that FOMC members shared their view. As a result, Warsh could have to justify additional hikes in the future if incoming data confirmed the shift.

They also said the muted foreign-exchange reaction to the employment data reinforced their view that a 25-basis-point hike would be reactionary, with markets effectively driving the Fed's policy path.

data.title: These low-priced stocks are flashing overbought signals
data.description:

Below is a list of the most overbought stocks trading under $10. The list is ranked based on their RSI.

The list is topped by Covalon Technologies Ltd. (CVALF), with an RSI of 85. RenovoRx (RNXT) comes in second with an RSI of 79. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum oscillator that measures the velocity and magnitude of price changes, plotting them on a scale from 0 to 100. RSI compares the magnitude of recent gains to recent losses over a chosen lookback period—typically 14 days.
